title: Getting started with rk8s
text: pod running ServiceAccount: kube() calls load_kube_config(), handles kubeconfig features ’re likely meet. KUBECONFIG can list several files; ’re merged first definition name wins. context’s default namespace used. Users can authenticate token token file, basic auth, client certificate (inline, file path relative kubeconfig appears ). Exec plugins work : EKS’s aws-iam-authenticator, GKE’s gke-gcloud-auth-plugin, AKS’s kubelogin OIDC helper. older oidc auth-provider, including refreshing token. Clusters can set proxy-url, tls-server-name insecure-skip-tls-verify. API server throttles (429), request retried whatever method. Server errors (500 504) dropped connections retried reads, since retrying write apply twice. Configuration$max_retries sets limit; default 3.
code: library(rk8s) k <- kube()                                   # $KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config # k <- kube(context = "my-dev") # k <- kube(config_file = "~/configs/prod.yaml") # k <- kube(namespace = "my-app")             # override the context namespace k <- kube(client = ApiClient$new(load_incluster_config()))

title: Getting started with rk8s
text: kube_apply() server-side apply. Give file, YAML JSON string, R list, one generated model objects. YAML string can hold several documents, goes right endpoint: Changes recorded field manager "rk8s" unless pass field_manager.
code: # From a file kube_apply(k, "deployment.yaml")  # From an R list (the most natural form for programmatic generation) kube_apply(k, list(   apiVersion = "v1", kind = "ConfigMap",   metadata = list(name = "demo"),   data = list(hello = "world") ))  # From a multi-doc YAML string kube_apply(k, " apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: {name: demo-cm} data: {greeting: hello} --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: {name: demo-svc} spec:   selector: {app: demo}   ports: [{port: 80, targetPort: 8080}] ")  # Force-take ownership of conflicting fields (server-side apply force): kube_apply(k, "deployment.yaml", force = TRUE)

title: Getting started with rk8s
text: timeout_seconds measured clock. API server ends watches schedule; rk8s reconnects happens returns time .
code: kube_scale(k, "deployment", "nginx", replicas = 5) kube_scale(k, "statefulset/postgres", replicas = 3)  cat(kube_logs(k, "nginx-abc", tail = 50)) kube_logs(k, "nginx-abc", container = "sidecar", follow = TRUE)  w <- kube_watch(k, "pods",   on_event = function(type, obj) {     message(type, " ", obj$metadata$name)     TRUE  # keep watching; return FALSE to stop   },   timeout_seconds = 30 ) w$end_reason   # "stop", "timeout" or "gone" (resourceVersion too old)  kube_delete(k, "pod", "nginx-abc") kube_delete(k, "deployment/nginx", grace_period = 0)

title: Getting started with rk8s
text: Custom resources need setup. rk8s finds API discovery, verbs take apiVersion kind cluster knows . small reconcile loop made-Foo resource looks like :
code: foos <- kube_list(k, "example.com/v1:Foo", namespace = "default") for (f in foos$items) {   if (is.null(f$status$ready) || !isTRUE(f$status$ready)) {     kube_apply(k, list(       apiVersion = "example.com/v1", kind = "Foo",       metadata = list(name = f$metadata$name),       status = list(ready = TRUE)     ))   } }

title: Getting started with rk8s
text: Listing everything every pass gets expensive. informer lists , keeps local copy current watch calls handlers things change. watch falls far behind, API server answers 410 Gone; informer lists , works changed away, fires on_delete anything disappeared.
code: inf <- Informer$new(   k$client,   resource_path = "/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods",   object_from_list = V1Pod$from_list ) inf$add_event_handler(   on_add    = function(obj) message("add: ", obj$metadata$name),   on_update = function(old, new) {     if (!identical(old$status$phase, new$status$phase))       message(new$metadata$name, ": ",               old$status$phase, " -> ", new$status$phase)   },   on_delete = function(obj) message("gone: ", obj$metadata$name) ) inf$run(stop_seconds = 120)  pods <- inf$lister() pods$get("nginx-abc", namespace = "default")   # cache lookup, no API call pods$list()

title: Getting started with rk8s
text: pod_exec() runs command gives output exit code: something interactive, pod_exec_open() returns PodExecSession can write write_stdin() read on_stdout(). Output arrives wait() pump() running. pod_port_forward() works like kubectl port-forward: need nanonext package. check API server’s certificate CA kubeconfig (system’s, kubeconfig none), log token. Kind, minikube kubeadm give default user client certificate token, ’ll get error use token instead:
code: r <- pod_exec(k$client, "default", "nginx-abc", c("ls", "-la", "/")) cat(r$stdout) r$exit_code  # With stdin pod_exec(k$client, "default", "nginx-abc", "cat", stdin_data = "hi\n")$stdout fwd <- pod_port_forward(k$client, "default", "nginx-abc", remote_port = 80) httr2::request(paste0("http://127.0.0.1:", fwd$port)) |> httr2::req_perform() fwd$close() # kubectl create serviceaccount rk8s-dev # kubectl create clusterrolebinding rk8s-dev --clusterrole=edit \ #   --serviceaccount=default:rk8s-dev cfg <- load_kube_config() cfg$api_key <- list(authorization = paste(   "Bearer", system("kubectl create token rk8s-dev", intern = TRUE))) k <- kube(client = ApiClient$new(cfg))

title: Getting started with rk8s
text: run one replica controller, want one work: callback runs, background process (started callr) keeps renewing lease. another replica takes lease, renewals keep failing, next leader$check() signals rk8s_leadership_lost condition. run_as_leader() catches , releases lease calls on_stopped_leading. Call leader$check() least per renew_deadline_seconds; ’s keeps two replicas acting leader time. ’d rather test interrupted, leader$is_leader() returns TRUE FALSE.
code: run_as_leader(   k$client,   lease_name = "my-controller",   lease_namespace = "kube-system",   identity = paste0(Sys.info()[["nodename"]], "-", Sys.getpid()),   on_started_leading = function(leader) {     message("leading")     repeat {       leader$check()      # signals once leadership is lost       reconcile_once()       Sys.sleep(5)     }   },   on_stopped_leading = function() message("stopped leading") )

text: kube() uses $KUBECONFIG (~/.kube/config) current context. context, config_file namespace arguments change . kube_apply() server-side apply, also takes file path R list: can name resource "pods", "pod", "po", "deployment/nginx", "apps/v1:Deployment" c("apps/v1", "Deployment"). title: Shared Informer - local cache of a resource, kept in sync via watch — Informer
text: Informer performs initial list resource, watches subsequent changes maintains local cache keyed namespace/name (just name cluster-scoped resources). Event handlers fire add/update/delete. R equivalent client-go's SharedIndexInformer. Informers canonical way build controllers: one watch feeds many handlers many Lister views, without consumer re-listing API server. Lifecycle: $run(stop_seconds = NULL) - block, streaming events cache. Returns stop_seconds wall-clock time elapse (whether events arrive) $stop() called handler. Safe re-invoke; informer resumes last observed resourceVersion. 410 Gone (watch fell far behind), informer re-lists reconciles cache fresh list: objects disappeared fire on_delete, new ones on_add, changed ones (different resourceVersion) on_update. Lists fetched pages page_size items (limit/continue). $has_synced() - TRUE initial list absorbed. $lister() - return Lister view current cache snapshot.

title: rk8s (development version)
text: pod_exec(), pod_exec_open(), pod_port_forward() pod_port_forward_open() now verify API server’s TLS certificate. previously used websocket package, accepts certificate hostname, bearer token sent impersonating server. now use nanonext (>= 1.10.3, Suggests instead websocket later), verify kubeconfig CA (system CA bundle) check hostname. insecure-skip-tls-verify still honoured set. Limitations new transport, reported clear error rather insecure connection: client-certificate-users need token exec / port-forward, tls-server-name supported . Sessions gain pump(timeout) dispatch incoming frames without blocking long; PodPortForwardSession gains is_closed(). Frames dispatched wait() pump() runs (, later event loop run).

title: rk8s (development version)
text: Typed create/replace calls (AppsV1Api$create_namespaced_deployment() generated write operations) failed 415 Unsupported Media Type: sent spec’s Content-Type: */* literally. Wildcards now sent application/json. kube_logs() CoreV1Api$read_namespaced_pod_log() failed 406 Acceptable (bare Accept: text/plain refused API server); */* now offered fallback. Untyped generated operations (logs, proxy, …) return text bodies strings instead failing parse JSON. pod_exec(stdin_data =) hung timeout: empty stdin frame sent EOF v4.channel.k8s.io protocol. Exec now offers v5.channel.k8s.io (Kubernetes 1.29+) close_stdin() sends stream-close message. Watch now delivers events arrive. previously read stream blocking 64 KB readBin(), small events held 64 KB accumulated server closed watch. Requires httr2 >= 1.1.0. Watch$stream(timeout_seconds =), kube_watch(timeout_seconds =) Informer$run(stop_seconds =) now real wall-clock limits. Previously watch reconnected forever server timeout, quiet resource calls never returned. Watch gains end_reason ("stop", "timeout", "gone") return_on_gone. Informer re-lists 410 Gone reconciles cache, firing on_delete objects removed disconnected (previously stayed cache forever), on_add new ones on_update changed ones. Lists paged (page_size, default 500). run_as_leader() can longer leave two leaders running: on_started_leading now receives leader handle must call leader$check() periodically; signals rk8s_leadership_lost lease lost renewals stop succeeding, run_as_leader() cleans calls on_stopped_leading(). Previously nothing noticed lost lease callback returned. background renewer now uses full connection settings (client certificates, token files, exec plugins) instead bearer token snapshot, failed cert-clusters expired exec tokens. Lease updates longer round-trip managedFields. lease released exit (release_on_exit), errors callback re-raised cleanup. Requires callr. Exec credential plugins (EKS, GKE, AKS/kubelogin, …) work : every call failed cache-key helper. now also receive input KUBERNETES_EXEC_INFO (provideClusterInfo support), keep stderr JSON parse, pass args env values containing spaces quotes intact, honour client certificate/key credentials, include installHint stderr errors, parse expiry timestamps fractional seconds offsets, re-run API server answers 401. kubeconfig user tokenFile: sent file path bearer token ($ partial matching read tokenFile token).

title: rk8s (development version)
text: KUBECONFIG several files merged like kubectl (first definition wins, relative paths resolve per file). context’s namespace read Configuration$namespace used default kube() (whose namespace argument now defaults NULL). -cluster config reads service account namespace. Cluster proxy-url tls-server-name honoured. OIDC auth-provider users supported, including id-token refresh; load_kube_config(persist_config = TRUE) writes refreshed tokens back. removed gcp/azure auth-providers give actionable error. Ordinary requests retried (Configuration$max_retries, default 3) 429 method 5xx/connection failures GET/HEAD, jittered backoff Retry-support. New Configuration$timeout. DynamicResource$list() (kube_list()) fetches pages.

title: rk8s 0.2.1
text: bridge child process now references internal bridge_one helper rk8s:::bridge_one since callr ships function body fresh R process unexported bindings aren’t injected. accept loop pumps websocket event loop via later::run_now waiting incoming TCP connections, instead busy-spinning blocking=FALSE accept. Local connections accepted non-blocking mode readBin returns immediately whatever kernel buffered. blocking=TRUE + socketSelect, local round-trip stretched seconds short HTTP exchanges macOS. Watch longer hangs chunks containing exactly one newline-terminated event. R’s strsplit("\\n", "\\n") returns c("") (drops trailing empty piece), previously made buffer-based parser keep waiting “”. Now detect trailing-newline case explicitly. Regression covered test-watch-buffer.R. New integration tests exec port-forward mint cluster-admin ServiceAccount token via TokenRequest websocket transport (can’t currently use client-cert auth) reachable cert-kubeconfigs like kind. Lives tests/integration/helper.R mint_token_client().

title: rk8s 0.2.0
text: New kube() session idiomatic verbs: kube_get(), kube_list(), kube_apply(), kube_delete(), kube_scale(), kube_logs(), kube_watch(). surface users want — never type V1Deployment$new(...) everyday work. Resource refs accept : kind alias ("pod", "po", "pods"), "kind/name" ("deployment/nginx"), explicit "apiVersion:Kind", c(apiVersion, Kind). Built-alias table covers common kubectl shortcodes (po, svc, deploy, sts, ds, rs, cm, sa, pv, pvc, ing, netpol, hpa, pdb, sc, crd, …). .data.frame() method rk8s_list returns tabular view (namespace / name / kind / age / status), kube_get(k, "pods") directly viewable. kube_apply() server-side apply (Content-Type: application/apply-patch+yaml) default, force = TRUE conflict resolution configurable field_manager.

title: rk8s 0.2.0
text: New pod_exec_open() / pod_exec() PodExecSession. Speaks v4.channel.k8s.io WebSocket, demuxes stdin/stdout/stderr/error/ resize channels, surfaces kubelet’s exit code. New pod_port_forward_open() PodPortForwardSession. subprotocol; per-port write() / on_data() API matching Python client’s design (local TCP listener required). depend websocket package (Suggests). Bearer-token auth — client-cert auth WebSocket yet supported.

title: rk8s 0.2.0
text: Critical correctness fix: generator now resolves $ref parameters spec$parameters emitting signatures. Prior versions silently dropped namespace, body, fieldManager, force, shared parameters every namespaced operation — making generated *_namespaced_* methods unusable. 944 operations regenerated. PATCH methods now accept optional content_type argument, defaulting spec’s first consumes entry. Pass application/apply-patch+yaml server-side apply, application/json-patch+json RFC 6902 patches. Argument-name collisions mixed-operations (notably connect_*_namespaced_pod_proxy_with_path, path path query parameter) disambiguated _query / _header / _body suffix preserving wire key.

title: rk8s 0.2.0
text: Windows: relaxed URL-assertion test-client-request.R decode query comparing, fixing Windows-failure caused httr2’s platform-dependent percent-encoding =. Vignette README rewritten lead verb API; typed layer documented drop-advanced cases. Integration test suite tests/integration/ running kind cluster, gated RK8S_E2E=1. New .github/workflows/integration.yaml runs push PR.

title: rk8s 0.1.0
text: Configuration + ApiClient — transport, auth (bearer, basic, client-cert, token-file, exec plugin), TLS, JSON (de)serialization, typed error translation. load_kube_config(), load_incluster_config(), list_kube_config_contexts(), new_client_from_config() — match semantics kubernetes.config Python client. Watch — streaming line-delimited JSON 410-Gone resume. Informer + Lister — client-go-style shared cache, initial list plus watch per-handler add/update/delete events. DynamicClient / DynamicResource — discovery-backed CRUD CustomResources untyped resource. run_as_leader() — leader election coordination.k8s.io/v1 Lease, optional callr-driven background renewer. ApiException + rk8s_api_error condition class. create_from_yaml(), parse_quantity().

title: rk8s 0.1.0
text: 62 typed API classes (CoreV1Api, AppsV1Api, BatchV1Api, NetworkingV1Api, RbacAuthorizationV1Api, …) covering 944 operations. 635 model classes (V1Pod, V1Deployment, V1ConfigMap, …) to_list() / from_list() JSON round-tripping. Unstructured scalar types (IntOrString, Quantity, Time, MicroTime, FieldsV1, RawExtension, JSON, Patch, JSONSchemaPropsOr*) emitted thin value wrappers. JSON-schema meta keys ($ref, $schema) mangled _ref, _schema R side preserving literal JSON key wire.

title: rk8s 0.1.0
text: tools/gen/generate.R + tools/gen/lib.R — reads Kubernetes OpenAPI v2 swagger.json writes R/gen_model_*.R R/gen_api_*.R. Idempotent; NAMESPACE exports managed sentinel lines.
